'''Harry Jeffrey Kimble''' (April 23, 1949 – September 2, 2024) was an American physicist who was the William L. Valentine Professor and professor of physics at [[Caltech]].<ref name="autogenerated2004">{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=H.%20Jeff%20Kimble&year=2004 |title=2004 Julius Edgar Lilienfeld Prize Recipient > H. Jeff Kimble |publisher=American Physical society |accessdate=June 21, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-05 |title=Caltech Mourns the Passing of Jeff Kimble (1949-2024) |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-mourns-the-passing-of-jeff-kimble-1949-2024 |access-date=2024-09-05 |website=California Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref> His research was in [[quantum optics]] and is noted for groundbreaking experiments in physics including one of the first demonstrations of [[Quantum teleportation|teleportation]] of a quantum state (first demonstration is disputed with [[Anton Zeilinger]]),<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Posteriori Teleportation | volume=394|issue=6696 |doi=10.1038/29674|journal=Nature|pages=840–841|arxiv=quant-ph/9810001|bibcode=1998Natur.394..840B|year=1998 |last1=Braunstein |first1=Samuel L. |last2=Kimble |first2=H. J. | s2cid=8920410}}</ref> [[Quantum gate|quantum logic gate]],<ref name=bell>{{cite web|last=Bell|first=Brian|title=H. Jeff Kimble to Receive Quantum Physics Award|url=https://www.caltech.edu/content/h-jeff-kimble-receive-quantum-physics-award|publisher=Caltech News|accessdate=January 2, 2014|archive-date=January 3, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103075716/http://www.caltech.edu/content/h-jeff-kimble-receive-quantum-physics-award|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the development of the first single atom [[laser]].<ref name="one-atom laser">{{cite journal|last=McKeever|first=J. |author2=Boca, A. |author3=Boozer, H. J. |author4=Buck, J. R. |author5=Kimble, H. J. |title=A One-Atom Laser in a Regime of Strong Coupling|journal=Nature|year=2003|volume=425|issue=6955 |pages=268–271|arxiv=quant-ph/0309199|doi=10.1038/nature01974 |pmid=13679909|bibcode=2003Natur.425..268M|s2cid=839175 }}</ref>  According to Elizabeth Rogan, [[Optical Society|OSA]] CEO,  "Jeff has led a revolution in modern physics through his pioneering research in the coherent control of the interactions of light and matter."<ref name=day>{{cite journal|last=Day|first=Brielle|title=OSA, DPG Name H. Jeff Kimble Winner of Herbert Walther Award|journal=Physics Today|doi=10.1063/PT.4.0496|year=2013|volume=2012 |issue=12 }}</ref>  Kimble's main research focus was in [[quantum information science]] and the [[quantum dynamics]] of [[Open system (systems theory)|open systems]].<ref name="autogenerated2004"/>

==Life and career==
Kimble graduated summa cum laude from [[Abilene Christian University]] in 1971 and earned his master's and doctoral degrees from [[University of Rochester]], culminating in 1979.<ref name="autogenerated2004"/> He was advised by [[Leonard Mandel]]. As a graduate student under Mandel, Kimble observed the first [[Photon antibunching|photon anti-bunching]].  He spent two years as a scientist for the [[General Motors Research Laboratories|General Motors Research Laboratory]] until 1979 when he joined the faculty at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=aps>{{cite web|title=2004 Julius Edgar Lilienfeld Prize Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=H.&last_nm=Kimble&year=2004|publisher=American Physical Society|accessdate=January 2, 2014}}</ref>   He moved to the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1989.<ref name=aps />

Kimble was a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows |url=http://php.aaas.org/about/aaas_fellows/list.php |publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] |access-date=June 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115191304/http://php.aaas.org/about/aaas_fellows/list.php |archive-date=January 15, 2014 }} Search by Name=K and Search By Section=Physics</ref> the [[American Physical Society]], and the [[Optical Society of America]]. He was elected as a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2002.<ref name="autogenerated2004"/>

Kimble died in [[Austin, Texas]] on September 2, 2024, at the age of 75.<ref>{{cite web |title=ACU Remembers: Dr. H. Jeff Kimble |url=https://acu.edu/2024/09/10/87068/ |access-date=10 September 2024 |website=Abilene Christian University}}</ref>
